title: Universal Volume Growth Bounds from Positive Intermediate Curvature
summary: Let $n,m$ be integers such that $n\geq2$ and $0\leq m\leq n-2$. Let $C_{m+1}$ denote the $(m+1)$-intermediate curvature introduced by Brendle--Hirsch--Johne. We prove that there are constants $ν(n,m),C(n,m)>0$ such that the following holds. If $(M^n,g)$ is complete and connected and, for $δ\geq 0$, \[ \mathrm{Ric}\geq-δ^2, \qquad C_{m+1}\geq 1, \] then \[ δR\leqν(n,m) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathrm{Vol} B_R(p) \leq C(n,m)R^m \quad \text{for every $p\in M$ and $R>0$.} \] In particular, taking $m=n-2$ and $δ=0$ gives Gromov's conjectured codimension-two volume growth estimate under…
